title: sim: accelerated simulator + `realm simulate`
criteria:
All code/comments/identifiers in English; no Thai text in this task.

== realm/sim/simulate.py ==
@dataclass Snapshot: day (float game days since the world epoch), avg_population: dict[str, float] (personality key -> average population of the bots of that personality, 0.0 when none), troops (int: sum of all Troop.count in the world), raids (int: number of Movement rows with mission 'raid' in the world, any status), failed_events (int: Events with status 'failed' in the world). @dataclass SimResult: snapshots: list[Snapshot], raids: int, failed_events: int.
`run_simulation(s: Session, cfg, *, days: float, speed: int, seed: int, bots: int, report_path: str | None = None, on_snapshot: Callable[[Snapshot], None] | None = None) -> SimResult`: uses ONE session; creates a fresh world with worlds.create_world(s, seed=seed, speed=speed, player_name='sim', tribe='stonehold', bot_count=bots, cfg=cfg, real_now=<fixed epoch datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)>) (the human village just sits idle and acts as a raid target; no real clock is used anywhere); rng = random.Random(seed); virtual `now` starts at the world epoch and the end is epoch + days*86400 seconds. Main loop until now >= end: next_event = min(due_at) of the world's pending events (SELECT min), next_bot = min(next_think_at) of the world's bot profiles, now = max(now, min(next_event, next_bot, end)) (treat None as 'infinity'); then process every due event: `while engine.worker.process_next(s, world, now, cfg): pass` and let the due bots think: `while bot.worker.think_due_bots(s, world, now, cfg, rng, limit=50) > 0: pass` (repeat the two steps until neither does anything for this `now`, then continue the loop; guard against infinite loops: if nothing was processed and the computed next time is not later than now, advance now by 1 second). Take a snapshot at day 0 and then every 12 game hours (a snapshot is taken when now crosses the next 12h boundary; make sure there is one at the very end too and no duplicate times); a snapshot computes the average population per personality from realm.services.ranking.get_ranking (population per player) grouped by BotProfile.personality, plus troops/raids/failed_events with COUNT queries; call on_snapshot(snapshot) and print one table row per snapshot with `print` ONLY via the callback/CLI, not inside run_simulation. Call s.flush() every iteration batch (commits are the caller's job). When report_path is given write a CSV: header `day,<personality keys in cfg order>,troops,raids,failed_events` and one row per snapshot. Return SimResult(snapshots, raids=last raids, failed_events=last failed).
== realm/cli.py ==
Implement `simulate` with options --days float (default 5), --speed int (default 1), --seed int (default 42), --bots int (default 30), --with-player-idle (flag, accepted for compatibility: the player is always idle), --report str (CSV path, optional). It runs `with session_scope() as s:` calling run_simulation with on_snapshot printing a fixed-width table row (columns: day, avg population per personality in cfg order, troops, raids, failed) after a header line, and committing `s.commit()` inside the callback so progress is saved; at the end print one summary line `raids=<n> failed_events=<n>`. Import run_simulation/load_config lazily inside the command. The command CREATES A NEW WORLD in the configured database (ends any running one): mention that in the command docstring. All other commands stay as they are.
== tests/test_simulate.py ==
DB tests with the rollback fixture `s` and `cfg` (conftest) - pass the fixture session to run_simulation. Cases (use days=1, speed=10, bots=5, seed=1 so they stay fast): returns SimResult with snapshots at days 0.0, 0.5 and 1.0 (3 snapshots, in order, day values within 1e-6); failed_events == 0; every snapshot's avg_population has the five personality keys of cfg.personalities; the sim never moves the real clock (monkeypatch realm.sim.simulate.time or datetime is NOT required; instead assert the world epoch equals datetime(2026,1,1,tzinfo=UTC)); the average population of each personality that has at least one bot at the end is >= its value at day 0 and, over all personalities with bots, the overall average at day 1 is strictly greater than at day 0 (bots build things); the CSV report written to tmp_path has the header `day,farmer,turtle,raider,expander,warlord,troops,raids,failed_events` (personality keys in cfg order) and 3 data rows; on_snapshot is called once per snapshot; determinism: two runs with the same seed give identical lists of (day, avg_population dict, troops, raids) snapshots (the second run creates another world in the same session, which is fine); run_simulation with days=0 returns only the day-0 snapshot; `realm simulate --help` lists the --days, --speed, --seed, --bots and --report options (typer CliRunner).
notes:
- Engine API: from realm.engine import worker as engine_worker; engine_worker.process_next(s, world, now, cfg) -> bool. Bot API: from realm.bot import worker as bot_worker; bot_worker.think_due_bots(s, world, now, cfg, rng, limit) -> int. Both exist and are tested.
- World/profile queries: select(func.min(Event.due_at)).where(Event.world_id == world.id, Event.status == 'pending'); select(func.min(BotProfile.next_think_at)).join(Player, Player.id == BotProfile.player_id).where(Player.world_id == world.id).
- Personality of a bot: BotProfile.personality; population per player: ranking.get_ranking(s, world.id, cfg) rows have player_id and population; map player_id -> personality from the BotProfile table.
- Boundary snapshots: next_boundary starts at epoch + 12h; while now >= next_boundary: take a snapshot labelled with day = (next_boundary - epoch).total_seconds()/86400 (so exact 0.5-day steps), then advance the boundary by 12h; after the loop take the final snapshot only if its day is not already present.
- No `datetime.now()` anywhere in realm/sim.
- Existing CLI tests (tests/test_smoke.py, tests/api/test_ws_cli.py) must keep passing.
